page.overview:
Who is Maiar?

The Maiar (singular Maia) were primordial spirits created to help the Valar shape the World. They were numerous, though not many were named.

Their chiefs were Eönwë, banner-bearer and herald of Manwë, and Ilmarë, the handmaid of Varda. Five of these spirits, in the Third Age, became the incarnated Wizards, also called the Istari.

Each of the Maiar is associated with one or more particular Vala of similar stock, though less powerful. For example, Eönwë is the herald of Manwë and Ilmarë the handmaiden of Varda, while Olórin (who was later named Gandalf) served both the Wind-king and the Star-Queen. Olórin's ways often took him also to the house of Nienna, and he learned from her pity and patience. Curumo (later known as Saruman) and Mairon (who later become a servant of Melkor, taking the name of Sauron) were both servants to Aulë, while Aiwendil (later known as Radagast) served Yavanna. Ossë, Uinen and Salmar, as spirits of the sea, belonged to Ulmo, Alatar (later known as a Blue Wizard); Pallando (later known as the other Blue Wizard) belonged to Oromë; and Melian served both Vána and Estë.

The Sun and Moon were also piloted by Maiar: Arien, a servant of Vána, was selected to guide the Sun, while Tilion, a hunter in the company of Oromë, was chosen to steer the Moon.
